title: Overview AI launches OV Spark, the inspection camera with an onboard agent named Sparky
summary: An onboard agent recommends inspection tools, explains its reasoning, and answers questions about what the line has been running, so a quality team can build and maintain an inspection without a vision specialist.
body_markdown:
SAN FRANCISCO, October 6, 2026 — Overview AI today launched OV Spark and OV Spark Pro, a new line of AI inspection cameras with an agentic layer that answers questions in plain English, allowing anyone, regardless of vision experience, to create an inspection recipe on their own.


Spark ships with ten inspection tools that can be mixed and matched in a single recipe. Seven are deep learning AI models: AI Trigger, Alignment, AI Classification, AI Segmentation, AI Count, AI OCR, and Anomaly Detection. The other three are ready to inspect out of the box, with the option to add images when an inspection needs training: Barcode, Measurement, and Color Match.


The recipe, model training, inference, judgment, PLC communication, image library, and the operator HMI all continue to run on the camera itself, a feature that's offered on every smart camera from Overview AI.


Overview AI has spent almost a decade improving the accuracy of its vision models. Even so, the gap customers ran into was consistency: which tool to use, and what to take from the production data, still came down to individual judgment.


This led to the creation of Sparky, the agent that lives on the Spark camera. Sparky gives teams a shared starting point for these judgment calls, so the reasoning behind an inspection is understood the same way by everyone who touches it.


> "We have been putting AI on factory floors since 2019, and the hardest part isn't the inspection itself. It's that every new line means another project, another specialist, another few weeks. Our mission is to catch every defect in every factory, so the camera has to carry that setup work itself. Spark is our best product at doing exactly that," said Chris Van Dyke, Co-Founder and CEO of Overview AI.


## Meet Sparky, an agent that guides decision making


Sparky explains which tools an inspection needs and why.


### Agentic tool selection


Sparky recommends the tools an inspection needs and explains the reasoning behind each one. When asked about a connector that must be confirmed to have twenty-four pins before it goes to a PLC, Sparky explains that the Alignment tool is needed to follow the part as it drifts, and the AI Count tool is needed to confirm every pin is accounted for.


### Agentic diagnostics


Sparky makes the capture library searchable in plain language, so a question about the previous shift returns a timeline of the captures, each with its verdict and the tool results associated with it.


### Agentic HMI builder


Sparky lays out the operator screen from a description of the data a station needs, using widgets built to show product metrics at a glance.


> "For years, manufacturers have told us the same thing: they have more inspection points than they have people qualified to set them up. Spark is our answer to that. A quality engineer who knows the part but has never trained a model can now get an inspection running on the line, and that changes who inside a plant can actually do this work," said Russell Nibbelink, Co-Founder and COO of Overview AI.


## New hardware


The 1.2MP OV Spark and the 5MP OV Spark Pro share the same sealed, all-in-one body, rated IP66 and small enough at 70 x 116 x 53 mm to drop into existing cells. The Spark can be powered over Ethernet through a PoE coupler.


> "We took seven years of what we learned deploying AI inspection in real plants and compressed it into one camera: Spark. We designed it on Qualcomm Dragonwing and put the whole agentic stack on the device. The camera recommends tools, reads production data, and lays out the operator screen itself. We've always run intelligence at the edge. Spark is the first product where that intelligence can support an expert in doing their job," said Xiaoyang Kao, Co-Founder and CTO of Overview AI.


## In production


Spark is running at Mansfield Engineered Components (MEC), a metal fabricator and contract manufacturer in Mansfield, Ohio, on an end-of-line station that had no formal inspection before it, only an operator's visual check. A missing washer is the most frequent defect on that line, and the inspection was built by a quality engineer who had never worked with a vision camera before joining the company a year ago. MEC has since moved the camera between two lines and is scoping a second Spark for a rivet curl and stenciled date code check.


OV Spark in production at MEC.


> "I'm a quality engineer with an industrial engineering degree, about a year into the job, and I had minimal experience with cameras before this. The part I expected to be difficult was the aligner, and it turned out to be pretty easy, because \[the camera\] tells you exactly what to do. I think we knocked it out of the park. \[Spark is\] reliable, easy to use, and easy to train your maintenance people on," said Logan Hoon, the quality engineer at MEC who built the inspection, on what it took to get the station running.


## About Overview AI


Overview AI builds deep-learning inspection cameras for manufacturers. The company was founded in 2018 by a team that ran production and quality systems at Tesla, where they managed thousands of daily defects across body assembly, battery production, and final vehicle inspection. They faced the choice every manufacturer faces, which is to inspect everything by hand and slow the line, or to sample and ship defects. They tried every vision system on the market. Traditional machine vision broke with every product change, and early AI needed months of training data. So they built the system they wished they had.


The OV Spark, OV10i, OV20i, and OV80i cameras and the OVX platform train and run inspection models on the camera, so quality teams deploy in days and retrain on the line without a PC or a data science team. Overview AI is headquartered in San Francisco with more than 80 people across 30 cities in 10 countries, and its cameras inspect hundreds of factories across more than 20 countries in automotive, electronics, medical devices, food and beverage, and industrial manufacturing. Co-founders Russell Nibbelink, Austin Appel, and Xiaoyang Kao were named to the Forbes 30 Under 30 list in Manufacturing and Industry. Overview is on a mission to catch every manufacturing defect in the world.


## Availability


OV Spark and OV Spark Pro are available now through Overview AI and its distribution partners. For specifications and to request a demonstration, visit[overview.ai/products/spark](https://www.overview.ai/products/ov-spark/) .
